scope: Pure canonical Gameplay Core seed/recipe variation, collision-clear authored-slot permutations, strict bounds and source binding, preserved five-template/player/persistence/Door limits, actual generated World 6502 speed execution and single-room emission. No proof of solvability or browser/hardware acceptance.

results.name: Default-off variation returns a detached unchanged canonical project
Same seed reproduces exact choices without modifying the project or live editor/emulator
Patrol speeds change only per-instance numeric overrides inside declared 1–4 bounds
Different seeds produce multiple actual speed recipes
Gameplay lock retains the complete prior selection while another seed is used
Recipes replay after JSON export and reject modified decisions
Recipe source binding rejects stale actor, collision, attribute, World links, and player start edits
Palette/CHR edits do not invalidate independently locked gameplay geometry
Compatible authored enemy/pickup slots permute without adding coordinates
Player, switches/doors, persistence owners, maps, links and template set remain exact
Placement refuses collision-intersecting slots and leaves that group intact
Placement refuses missing collision evidence instead of assuming empty space
Single-room placement follows metatile reconciliation instead of trusting stale empty collision
Placement excludes body extents beyond map, Room, or screen edges
A placement permutation cannot move patrols outside their own authored bounds
An aliased speed/bound parameter cannot masquerade as a bounded patrol variation
Different colliders or placement owners cannot share slots
Disabled or custom behaviors are left unmodified and explicitly unavailable
Item-value requests report unavailable and preserve boolean pickup semantics
Disabled Gameplay Core stays disabled and has explicit unavailable domains
Actor and persistent RAM capacity refusals are atomic
Malformed seeds/options and invalid canonical values refuse before mutation
Toggling placement cannot change domain-separated patrol speed choices
Actual emitted World ROM and 6502 patrol movement reflect the chosen speed
Shuffled pickup source slots reach the actual compiled actor coordinates and preserve collection binding
A single-room candidate preserves its backend and emits changed patrol speed
